name_en: Yamato zoni — New Year mochi soup in white miso, eaten with sweetened soybean flour
summary_ja: 丸餅と祝だいこん、里芋、豆腐を白味噌仕立てのだしで煮た奈良の雑煮。餅を取り出して砂糖入りのきな粉につけて食べる家庭が多く、豆腐は白壁の蔵、里芋は子孫繁栄を願う具材とされている。
summary_en: Nara-style New Year mochi soup with round rice cakes, thin celebratory daikon, taro, and tofu in a white miso broth. In many households the mochi is lifted out and dipped in sweetened soybean flour; the tofu is said to stand for a white-walled storehouse, the taro for family prosperity.
source_publisher: 農林水産省「うちの郷土料理」

name_en: Kashiwa no sukiyaki — chicken sukiyaki simmered in a sweet soy broth
summary_ja: 関西で食用鶏を指す「かしわ」の名がついた奈良のすき焼き。牛が天神さんの守護神とされることから、天満宮の秋祭りでは牛の代わりに鶏のすき焼きが食べられてきたとされ、割り下で白菜や焼き豆腐と煮る。
summary_en: A Nara-style sukiyaki named for kashiwa, the Kansai word for chicken meat. Because cattle are held sacred to the deity of the Tenjin shrines, chicken sukiyaki is said to have been eaten in place of beef at their autumn festivals, simmered with napa cabbage and grilled tofu in a sweet soy broth.
source_publisher: 農林水産省「うちの郷土料理」

name_en: Asuka nabe — chicken and vegetables simmered in a milk-enriched broth
summary_ja: 鶏肉と季節の野菜を牛乳とだし汁で煮込む明日香村の鍋。飛鳥時代に唐からもたらされた乳製品が宮中に伝わり、後に飼っていた鶏の肉を牛乳で煮た精進料理が起源とされ、昭和初期に今の形になったという。
summary_en: A hot pot from Asuka Village of chicken and seasonal vegetables simmered in milk and dashi. It is said to trace to a dairy product brought from Tang China in the Asuka period and later reworked by monks who simmered their chickens in milk, taking its present form around the early Showa era.
source_publisher: 農林水産省「うちの郷土料理」
